events.label: Loading
events.detail: Estimated deepest knee bend before upward reach. Review the frame; this is not a validated trophy-position label.

events.label: Upward reach
events.detail: Highest tracked hitting wrist. This does not establish ball contact.

stages.label: Setup
stages.detail: A relatively still body position before the serve movement; not a stance-quality score.

evidence.observation: A relatively still setup is visible before the upward movement.
evidence.cue: Use this frame as your starting position when replaying the complete sequence.

stages.label: Tossing-arm rise
stages.detail: Estimated tossing-arm rise. Ball release and toss apex are not measured.

evidence.observation: The tossing wrist rises above shoulder level during preparation in this view.
evidence.cue: Replay the arm rise into loading and check how the two movements overlap.

stages.label: Loading
stages.detail: Deepest tracked knee bend before upward reach; not a verified trophy position.

evidence.observation: At loading, the left knee angle is 149° and the right is 128° in this view.
evidence.cue: Replay loading into the upward swing and watch the knees begin to straighten.

stages.label: Upward swing / reach
stages.detail: Loading and reach are visible, but intervening tracking is incomplete. Their timing does not establish the swing path.

stages.label: Follow-through
stages.detail: Observed arm descent after reach. Missing wrist samples are not interpolated; visible elbow and torso recovery can establish this stage.

evidence.observation: The hitting elbow lowers after reach while the visible torso moves into recovery; the wrist is occluded.
evidence.cue: Replay reach into the descending arm and body recovery.

stages.label: Finish / recovery
stages.detail: Observed downward arm movement and recovery after reach. Complete stillness, landing and foot-ground contact are not required or established.

evidence.observation: The downward arm sequence has continued into visible recovery after the reach.
evidence.cue: Review the recovered arm and body position at the end of the motion.
